newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Police clash with protesters in Ecuador capital.
newsitem.headline: Police clash with protesters in Ecuador capital.

text.p: Riot police fired volleys of tear gas into crowds of demonstrators in downtown Quito on Friday to prevent them from occupying the main plaza outside Ecuador's presidential palace.

Ecuadorean televison showed dramatic images of police, backed by armored personnel carriers, firing large quantities of tear gas into the historic city center as protesters tried to clamber over rolls of barbed wire blocking access to Independence Square.
A young girl was overcome by the fumes that wafted over the ornate Carondelet presidential palace but there were no immediate reports of serious injuries.
But national television said at least two demonstrators were hurt earlier in the Pacific coast city of Guayaquil when police broke up a clash between rival political factions.

The protests in Quito were the first since late Thursday when thousands of people took to the streets to demand that President Abdala Bucaram, ousted by Congress Thursday night, abandon the presidential palace.
Defense Minister Victor Bayas said Friday that the government had decided to declare a nationwide state of emergency in an attempt to quell the protests and preserve law and order.
